speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You have chronic diarrhea and lower abdominal discomfort; to begin our investigation, how long have these symptoms been present, and have you noticed any blood, mucus, or fever?

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Irritable Bowel Syndrome with Diarrhea (IBS-D) with a differential diagnosis of infectious colitis (Campylobacter or Shigella) given the camping exposure. The relief of pain with defecation and presence of mucus are classic for IBS, though the recent illness of a campmate raises concern for an acute infectious trigger or post-infectious IBS.
